g.text: ↑ anomaly of the season's mean daily minimum (°C, vs 1850–1900)

svg.text: Uppsala (GHCN-D SWE00139148), daily minimum temperature, seasonal means. Each season is compared with its own 1850–1900 mean (the IPCC's pre-industrial baseline). All
four seasons have warmed by about 3 °C (2.9 in autumn to 3.6 in spring), about twice the global land average, partly because Uppsala grew around the thermometer (see the
caveats). Winter dots scatter over ±5 °C, summer dots over ±2 °C: that spread is the noise the next graph measures the warming against. The record has gaps (1868–83, 1922–30,
1945–58); the running mean bridges them. Click a dot for the station's NOAA record.
